Neutral Citation  2024:CGHC:13439  1  NAFR  HIGH COURT OF CHHATTISGARH, BILASPUR  M. Cr. C. (A) No. 1465 of 2023  Niranjan Tigga, son of Mangra Tigga, aged about 32 years,
 resident of Village- Cherna Bera, Post & Police Station - Namkum,
 District - Ranchi (Jharkhand)

---- Applicant  Versus  State of Chhattisgarh, through the Station House Officer, Police  Station- Mahila Thana, Ambikapur, District Surguja (C.G.)
 ----Non-applicant For Applicant : Mr. Gurudeo I. Sharan, Advocate.
For Non-applicant : Ms. Isha Jijodiya, Panel Laywer.
Hon'ble Mr. Justice Naresh Kumar Chandravanshi  Order On Board 16-04-2024
Heard.

1. 
The applicant has filed this application for grant of anticipatory bail as he is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No. 16/2023 registered at police station Mahila Thana, Ambikapur,
District - Surguja (C.G.) for commission of offence punishable under Section 376 (2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code.

2. Facts of the case, in brief, are that complainant, who is aged about 24 years, came in contact with the applicant through Facebook in the year 2022 and since then the applicant and complainant used Niranjan Tigga vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192505947/

sentences.text: to talk with each other through mobile
and the applicant has informed her that he is Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:13439 posted in Army at Delhi Base Camp.

In the month of September, 2022,
the applicant came to Ambikapur and on being called by him, complainant met with him and they lived together in a Hotel for one day, thereafter, the applicant returned to his duty and after about 15 days, applicant sent railway ticket to complainant for visiting Delhi, upon which, complainant alongwith her friend went to Delhi, where they resided together for about 15 days, in between, they performed marriage in Lotus Temple, Delhi.
After about one week, complainant returned to Ambikapur alongwith her friend.

It is further alleged that after about two days, applicant came at Ambikapur where he resided with the complainant and in the meantime, applicant made physical relation with the complainant from 04.09.2022 to 24.01.2023.
Subsequently, applicant refused to keep the complainant with him, whereas, the complainant was carrying four months' pregnancy from the applicant.
Based on above facts, present crime has been registered against the applicant.
3. Learned counsel appearing for the applicant would submit that the applicant, who is posted in Army at Delhi Base Camp, still wants to keep the complainant as his wife.
It is further submitted that the applicant is in Government job and at present his posting is at Laddakh, where he cannot keep complainant alongwith him.

As the complainant was pressuring the applicant to keep her with him at his place of posting, which was not possible, only on this count, present FIR has been lodged by the complainant , hence, the applicant may be extended the benefit of anticipatory bail.
Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:13439 4.

Per contra, learned counsel for the State while opposing the bail application filed by the applicant would submit that applicant has sexually exploited the complainant and despite getting marriage with her, he is not ready to keep her with him, therefore, the applicant is not entitled for grant of anticipatory bail.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

6. Having heard learned counsel for the parties, having regard to the facts & circumstances of the case, particularly, considering the fact that applicant is said to be posted at Laddakh as Army Personnel; and further considering the fact that FIR was lodged merely because of inability of applicant to keep complainant with him, thus, considering totality of the facts; this Court is of the view that it is a fit case to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Accordingly, the application is allowed.

It is directed that in the event of arrest, the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- with one surety for the like sum to the satisfaction of the officer arresting him and he shall abide by all the following terms and conditions:
(i) that the accused/applicant shall make himself available for interrogation before the concerned Investigating Officer as and when required.
(ii) that the accused/applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement,
threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him/her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer;
Niranjan Tigga vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192505947/
2 Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:13439 (iii) that the accused/applicant shall not act, in any manner, which will be prejudicial to fair and expeditious trial; and (iv) that the applicant shall appear before the trial Court on each and every date given to him by the said Court till disposal of the trial.
Certified copy, as per rules.
Sd/-
(Naresh Kumar Chandravanshi) Judge Amit/-
